findings.title: Retry-count deletion is not scoped to SMS reminders
findings.body: The deleteMany OR's second branch only checks retryCount > 1, without method: WorkflowMethods.SMS (and without scheduled: false). Because WorkflowReminder rows are shared by EMAIL, SMS and WHATSAPP methods, any non-SMS reminder whose retryCount ever exceeds 1 will be deleted by this SMS cron, losing its referenceId/cancellation handle even though this job never processed it. The SMS-only condition from the original first branch does not carry over to the second OR branch.

findings.title: Missing recipient or empty message never increments retryCount
findings.body: The retry increment only happens inside `if (message?.length && sendTo)` when twilio.scheduleSMS returns falsy, or in the catch block. If sendTo is null/empty (e.g. booking has no smsReminderNumber / step has no sendTo) or the rendered message is empty, neither branch runs: the reminder stays scheduled:false with retryCount 0 and is re-fetched and re-processed on every cron run until its scheduledDate passes. This is one of the permanent-failure modes the PR is meant to bound, so those reminders are still retried indefinitely.

findings.title: Unhandled update in catch block can abort the whole cron run
findings.body: The catch block now awaits prisma.workflowReminder.update without any nested error handling. If that update rejects (e.g. the reminder was deleted by the top-of-run deleteMany of a concurrent invocation, a booking-cancellation cleanup, or a transient DB error - Prisma throws P2025 for a missing record), the exception propagates out of the per-reminder loop, the handler returns 500, and all remaining unscheduled reminders in the batch are never processed in this run. Previously the catch only logged and the loop continued.

findings.title: Retry increment uses stale snapshot instead of atomic increment
findings.body: Both increments write `retryCount: reminder.retryCount + 1` using the value read by the earlier findMany. If two cron invocations (or overlapping executions of the same invocation window) process the same unscheduled reminder concurrently, both read the same count and both write the same count+1, losing an increment; likewise a concurrent successful scheduling can be overwritten in effect because the failure writer does not condition on scheduled:false. This lets a permanently failing reminder be attempted more than the intended two times and makes the >1 deletion threshold unreliable. Use Prisma's atomic `{ increment: 1 }` (ideally guarded by scheduled:false).
